en: I bow to the one whose holy lotus feet are served by the king of the gods, who wears a serpent as his sacred thread, who has the moon as his crest-jewel, who is the source of compassion,
and who is clothed only by the directions, being saluted by hosts of yogis such as Nārada.
I worship Kālabhairava, the sovereign of the city of Kāśī;
the supreme blue-throated one, who possesses three eyes, who shines like ten million suns, who is the savior from the ocean of worldly existence, and the bestower of desired objects.

I worship Kālabhairava, the lord of the city of Kāśī, the lotus-eyed one who is both time and beyond time, the imperishable one whose weapon is the trident; I worship the primordial cause who holds the trident, the ṭaṅka-axe, the noose, and the staff in his hands.

I worship Kālabhairava, the lord of the city of Kāśī, whose body is dark-hued, the primordial god, the imperishable and free from all affliction; the master of formidable prowess, who delights in the wondrous tāṇḍava dance.
Bestowing both worldly enjoyment and liberation, possessing a body praised by the world,
standing as the refuge for devotees, and embodying the form of all the worlds;
with a beautiful waist adorned with a girdle of tinkling golden bells.
I worship Kālabhairava, the sovereign of the city of Kāśī;
the protector of the bridge of dharma, the destroyer of the path of adharma, the liberator from the noose of karma, the bestower of supreme bliss, and the all-pervading Lord.
I worship Kālabhairava, the sovereign lord of the city of Kāśī, whose entire body is adorned with a noose of golden serpents,
and whose pair of feet is beautiful with the luster of jeweled sandals.

I worship Kālabhairava, the sovereign lord of the city of Kāśī, who is eternal, without a second, the beloved deity, stainless, the destroyer of the pride of Death, and the liberator from fearsome fangs.
He whose laughter splits the continuous series of the lotus-egg's interior,
who destroys the web of sins through the casting of his gaze, who possesses a fierce command,
who bestows the eight siddhis, and who wears a garland of skulls;
I worship Kālabhairava, the sovereign lord of the city of Kāśī,
the leader of the hosts of spirits, the bestower of vast fame,
the all-pervading one who purifies the merit and sin of those residing in Kāśī.

I worship Kālabhairava, the ancient Lord of the World and sovereign of the city of Kāśī, who is skilled in the path of ethics. Men certainly go into the presence of the feet of Kālabhairava— the means for liberation through knowledge, the increaser of manifold merit,
and the destroyer of sorrow, delusion, wretchedness, greed, anger,
and fever.
I worship Kālabhairava, the sovereign lord of the city of Kāśī.
